subject.title: fix(cron): bound cron quarantine sidecar file reads

question: What persisted-data lifecycle should cron quarantine recovery archives use before overflow rotation is allowed to land?
rationale: The branch correctly avoids silently deleting recovery data, but retaining an unlimited number of 8-MiB files transfers the availability failure from memory to disk; choosing explicit operator cleanup, a documented finite retention rule, or accepting that risk is a product and operations policy decision.

options.title: Doctor-managed archive cleanup
options.body: Keep archives for recovery, surface their count and size through Doctor, and make cleanup an explicit operator action.

options.title: Approve finite automatic retention
options.body: Adopt a documented count or age limit with focused upgrade and data-retention tests, accepting automatic deletion as an intentional policy.

options.title: Do not rotate sidecars yet
options.body: Land only the bounded reader and actionable failure until a recovery-data lifecycle is designed.

recommendation.title: Doctor-managed archive cleanup
recommendation.body: Keep archives for recovery, surface their count and size through Doctor, and make cleanup an explicit operator action.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied timeline provides the only concrete maintainer-side signal around the archive-policy discussion.
